answer: Each agent periodically submits an opal‑colored proof of unique work—a puzzle whose solution is hashed with a fresh seed and the agent’s immutable ivory‑signed identity, then recorded on the ledger’s terrace of consensus blocks. The protocol rejects any duplicate or near‑duplicate output by comparing the new hash against recent entries, forcing a sybil to produce entirely distinct puzzles for each fake identity. Because each distinct puzzle incurs the full computational cost of the base task, the attacker’s expense grows linearly with the number of identities, quickly becoming prohibitive.
